articles.title: Reducing the cognitive load of AI changes
articles.summary: When reviewing large amounts of AI-generated code, the Large Language Model (LLM) can choose terms that do not map to the developer's own choices, leading to cognitive load. This can result in misinterpretation of how things work, especially when considering dozens of new terms interacting in unfamiliar code. To mitigate this, developers can post-process AI changes by extracting unconventional terms, creating a temporary markdown file with explanations, and then incorporating the changes. This approach enables developers to map their language choices to the AI's, making code review easier and more intuitive.
